title: Continuous Data Collection
description: The wearable device continuously captures sensitive user biometric data (heart rate, step counts, GPS position) without explicit, ongoing consent from the user.

title: Inference of Sensitive Information
description: The continuous collection of GPS position and timestamps allows for the inference of the user's precise location and movement patterns over time.

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Policy
description: The device's continuous data collection may violate the user's privacy policy if the user has not explicitly agreed to the continuous monitoring.

title: Data Minimization
description: The device collects more data (continuous telemetry) than is strictly necessary for the stated purpose (e.g., basic health monitoring).

title: Data Processing
description: The device processes raw sensor data (heart rate, step counts) without any aggregation or anonymization, making it directly accessible to the user.

title: User Awareness
description: The user is not aware that their continuous biometric data is being collected and stored by the device.

title: No Consent
description: The user has not given explicit consent for the continuous collection of sensitive biometric data.

title: Data Access

title: Data Disclosure

title: Inappropriate Data Exposure
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) is transmitting sensitive health data (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) to the Health Log Store (DS1). This flow involves the direct transfer of personal health information, which is a sensitive data type under LINDDUN Pro.

title: Data Inappropriateness
description: The data being transferred (health logs) is not relevant to the purpose of the Health Log Store (DS1). The store is likely intended for administrative or system-level logging, not personal health data. This creates a mismatch between the data and the data store's intended use.

title: Data Discontinuity
description: The data flow from the Companion App (P2) to the Health Log Store (DS1) is not a direct data flow. The data is likely stored locally on the device or in a temporary buffer before being written to DS1. This creates a data discontinuity where the data is not immediately available to the store.

title: Uncertainty in Data Classification
description: It is uncertain whether the data being written to DS1 is truly classified as 'Health Data' under the specific LINDDUN Pro classification scheme. While the data is personal, the specific categorization might depend on the exact definition of 'Health Data' in the current model.

title: Location Data Exposure
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) writes GPS location traces with timestamps to the Location History Store (DS2). This action exposes sensitive personal location data to unauthorized access.

title: Timestamp Leakage
description: The App includes precise timestamps in the location data. This allows adversaries to correlate location events with specific times, potentially revealing the user's movement patterns and habits.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: The App may modify or delete location data before writing it to the store, leading to inaccurate or incomplete records of the user's movements.

title: Data Duplication
description: The App may duplicate location data multiple times before writing it to the store, increasing the volume of sensitive data processed.

title: Uncertainty in Data Classification
description: The classification of the data as 'sensitive personal location data' is uncertain. The App may store location data that is not actually sensitive, or vice versa.
uncertainty_note: The sensitivity of the data is not definitively established by the App's internal logic.

title: Data Leakage
description: Inferred health-condition risk indicators and trend flags are returned to the Companion Mobile App without explicit consent or a clear data minimization justification. The app may use this data for targeted advertising or profiling, which is not permitted under the DPA.

title: Inference Risk
description: The process 'Health Analytics Service' performs inference on user data (health-condition risk indicators) to generate insights. This inference process itself may violate privacy principles if the inference is not necessary for the stated purpose.

title: Data Minimization
description: The process returns routine summaries and trend flags, which may be considered excessive data for the purpose of providing health insights, potentially violating the principle of data minimization.

title: User Consent
description: The Companion Mobile App may not have obtained explicit, informed consent from the user to receive and process inferred health insights, which is a fundamental privacy requirement.

title: Inference of Eating Disorder Risk
description: The process P2 infers eating disorder risk signals from user data without explicit user consent or a clear, opt-in mechanism for the user to opt out.
assumptions: The system assumes that the user's behavior (e.g., missed meals, irregular patterns) is a reliable indicator of an eating disorder.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the inference logic is robust enough to reliably distinguish between normal fluctuations and actual eating disorder signals without additional validation.

assumptions: The system assumes that the user's health status (e.g., blood glucose levels, medication adherence) is a reliable indicator of diabetes risk.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the inference logic is robust enough to reliably distinguish between normal fluctuations and actual diabetes risk without additional validation.

title: Display of Personal Health Information
description: The external entity EE1 (User) is displaying personal health information (eating disorder or diabetes risk signals) to the user.
assumptions: The user is viewing their own health data, which is sensitive and potentially indicative of their condition.

title: Data Infiltration
